source.title: 5-HT modulation of a medial septal circuit tunes social memory stability

confidence_rationale: High-quality circuit dissection (optogenetics + slice physiology + behaviour) from a leading lab showing that median-raphe serotonergic input bidirectionally controls hippocampal-circuit memory STABILITY. It is a strong demonstration of the general principle the layer needs -- median raphe 5-HT modulating a hippocampal-representational-stability parameter -- but the receptor implicated is 5-HT1B (on medial-septum neurons), not 5-HT1A, and the locus is the MS->dCA2 social-memory circuit, not the CA1/DG aversive-terrain the layer names. Confidence capped accordingly.
failure_signatures: The modulation is mediated by 5-HT1B on medial septal neurons and targets dCA2 social-memory stability, NOT 5-HT1A on CA1/DG aversive terrain -- so this paper supports the GENERIC 'median raphe 5-HT tunes hippocampal representational stability' principle but not the layer's specific 5-HT1A receptor or its aversive-basin construct.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Median-raphe serotonergic terminals in the medial septum bidirectionally regulate social-memory stability: novel social interaction increases activity in dCA2-projecting MS neurons and induces glutamatergic plasticity onto dCA2 pyramidal cells; 5-HT enhances the activity of these MS cells (via 5-HT receptors on MS neurons), and optogenetic manipulation of median-raphe 5-HT terminals in MS bidirectionally controls memory stability.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-085 holds that median-raphe serotonin shapes hippocampal-terrain geometry and the depth/stability of attractor basins. Wu et al. give a concrete instance of median-raphe 5-HT setting a hippocampal-circuit STABILITY parameter (here, how stable a social-memory representation is), which is the same family of computation REE attributes to the terrain plane -- serotonin tuning how firmly a hippocampal representation holds.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Receptor and target both differ from the layer's specific claim: the effect is 5-HT1B-mediated on medial-septum neurons modulating dCA2 SOCIAL-MEMORY stability, not 5-HT1A on CA1/DG modulating AVERSIVE-basin depth. This supports the generic principle (median raphe 5-HT -> hippocampal representational stability) but is at best indirect support for the 5-HT1A aversive-terrain assignment, and could even be read as a competing receptor account.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; optogenetics + slice electrophysiology + social-memory behaviour; median raphe -> medial septum -> dCA2 circuit.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high (Nature, rigorous circuit dissection). Mapping_fidelity low because the receptor (5-HT1B) and construct (social-memory stability, not aversive-basin depth) both differ from the layer's specific 5-HT1A/terrain claim. Included as principle-level support with an explicit divergence flag.
